name: Question_det
questiontext:
Let \(A \in M_{4 \times 4}(\mathbb{R})\) be a matrix with \(det(A)=7\).

Check ALL of the correct statements:

[[input:ans]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Since \(\det(A)\ne 0\), \(A\) is invertible; from this we find how many solutions \(Ax=b\) has for each \(b\), and then go over the options.
Step 1 — A is invertible
A square matrix is invertible if and only if its determinant is nonzero. Here \(\det(A)=7\ne 0\), so \(A\) is invertible.
Step 2 — Exactly one solution for every b
For every \(b\in \mathbb{R}^4\), \(x=A^{-1}b\) is a solution, since \(A(A^{-1}b)=b\). It is the only one: if \(Ax=b\), multiplying by \(A^{-1}\) on the left gives \(x=A^{-1}b\). So for every \(b\) the equation has exactly one solution.
Step 3 — The options
  • For some \(b \in \mathbb{R}^4\) the equation \(Ax=b\) has exactly one solution. — correct: in fact every b gives exactly one solution (Step 2).
  • For some vector \(b \in \mathbb{R}^4\) the equation \(Ax=b\) has infinitely many solutions. — incorrect: no b: the solution is always unique (Step 2).
  • For some vector \(b \in \mathbb{R}^4\) the equation \(Ax=b\) has no solution. — incorrect: \(A^{-1}b\) is always a solution (Step 2).
  • For all vectors \(b \in \mathbb{R}^4\) the equation \(Ax=b\) has at least one solution. — correct: \(A^{-1}b\) is a solution (Step 2).
  • For some vector \(b \in \mathbb{R}^4\) the equation \(Ax=b\) has exactly 7 solutions. — incorrect: the number of solutions is always 1; the value of the determinant does not count solutions.

Answer: the statement with exactly one solution for some b, and the statement with at least one solution for all b.
